message: _decode_token falls back to jwt.decode with verify_signature=False and 'none' algorithm, so any attacker can forge an unsigned token for any user_id and gain full authentication.
JWT signed with hardcoded weak secret 'secret', allowing offline token forgery once the key is known from source.
Login query built with f-string interpolation of username, enabling SQL injection (e.g. auth bypass via OR 1=1).
Register INSERT built with f-string interpolation of username, enabling SQL injection / account creation with attacker-controlled values.
update-password takes user_id from the request body and changes that user's password without verifying the current user or current password, letting any authenticated user take over any account.

Password reset token is md5(username), fully predictable by an attacker, and is additionally leaked in the response as 'debug_token', enabling trivial account takeover; reset_password (line 208) accepts it.
yaml.load with yaml.Loader on user-supplied YAML allows arbitrary Python object construction and remote code execution.
Passwords hashed with unsalted MD5, which is cryptographically broken and fast to brute-force.
Session token cookie set with httponly=False and secure=False, exposing the JWT to XSS-based theft and non-TLS transmission.
/api/me returns the entire stored profile, including PII such as SSN and date of birth, to any authenticated user.
update_profile assigns arbitrary JSON fields to the user (e.g. email) with no validation, allowing email takeover that undermines account recovery.
Transactions query built with f-string interpolation of the user_id query parameter, enabling SQL injection.
get_transactions reads user_id from the request instead of the authenticated user, allowing any user to view any other user's transactions.
Transaction search query built with f-string interpolation of the description search term, enabling SQL injection.
Transfer allows negative amounts: the 'balance < amount' check is bypassed so a negative amount credits the sender and debits the receiver, duplicating money.
fastpay performs the transfer with no balance check at all, allowing unlimited overdraft and money creation.
share_cost debits an arbitrary user supplied via from_user_id (and has no balance check), letting any user drain any other account.

Unauthenticated receipt page is rendered with an f-string HTML template that injects user-controlled transaction fields (e.g. description) without escaping, enabling stored XSS; the endpoint also has no authentication.
generate_report concatenates user-supplied report_type/date_range into a shell command executed with shell=True, allowing arbitrary command execution.
svc_status runs os.popen on a shell string containing the user-supplied 'unit' parameter, allowing arbitrary command execution.
net_check runs 'ping -c 3 {host}' with shell=True using the user-supplied target, allowing arbitrary command execution.
resolve_name runs nslookup via Popen with shell=True on the user-supplied domain, allowing arbitrary command execution.
probe-url fetches a fully user-controlled URL server-side with no allowlist, allowing SSRF against internal services and cloud metadata.
fetch-avatar fetches a user-controlled URL (SSRF) with TLS verification disabled (verify=False), allowing internal probing and MITM of responses.
download-statement joins the user-supplied filename onto /app/statements/ with no sanitization, allowing read of arbitrary files via ../ traversal.
view-log opens /var/log/{file} with a user-supplied filename, allowing arbitrary file read via ../ traversal.
import-data parses user XML with lxml XMLParser(resolve_entities=True, no_network=False), enabling XXE file read and external entity fetch.
import-session unpickles base64-decoded user data with pickle.loads, allowing remote code execution.
update_user applies every JSON field via setattr on the User model, allowing any authenticated user to set role='admin', change balances, or overwrite password hashes (privilege escalation).
preview-email passes the user-supplied template directly to render_template_string, allowing SSTI and remote code execution.
/api/redirect follows a fully user-controlled URL parameter, enabling open redirect / phishing.
search-users compiles the user-supplied regex with re.match over all usernames, enabling catastrophic backtracking DoS and dumping full user dicts.
compute evaluates the user-supplied 'formula' with Python eval(), allowing arbitrary code execution.
run-script executes user-supplied code with exec(), allowing arbitrary code execution.
format-data compiles and exec()s user-supplied 'format' code, allowing arbitrary code execution.
Integrity verification uses SHA-1, a broken hash that is weak for collision-resistant integrity checks.
API tokens generated as MD5 of a user-controlled seed, which is predictable and unsuitable as an authentication token.
Root/master password 'R00tAccess@2026#' is hardcoded in source, granting admin access to anyone who knows it.
Admin-only action guarded only by an assert on current_user.role, which is stripped under python -O and trivially spoofable via the mass-assignment flaw.
list_all_users returns every user's password_hash and full profile (including SSN) to any authenticated user.
delete_user (and other admin endpoints) is gated only by token_required with no role check, letting any authenticated user delete arbitrary users.
export-report writes user-supplied content to a predictable world-readable /tmp path and serves it back, enabling file planting/injection via /tmp.
dashboard-data returns hardcoded ADMIN_API_KEY and AWS_ACCESS_KEY in the API response to any authenticated user.
Multiple live-looking production secrets hardcoded in source (admin API key, AWS access/secret keys, Stripe, DB password, SendGrid, GitHub token, JWT private key, Slack webhook).
upload-avatar saves using the raw client filename with os.path.join and os.makedirs(dirname), allowing traversal to write files outside the upload directory.
Avatar upload performs no file-type or content validation, allowing upload of executable/web content that is later served by /uploads.
serve_upload joins the unvalidated URL path segment onto UPLOAD_DIR, allowing read of arbitrary files via ../ and serving them (including as images for stored-XSS/phishing payloads).
User password hashing/verification uses unsalted MD5, which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to rainbow-table/brute-force attacks.
Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source, enabling session/CSRF token forgery and weakening any signing that relies on it.

after_request reflects an arbitrary Origin header in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing any origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests.
Flask runs with debug=True, exposing the Werkzeug interactive debugger which allows remote code execution.
Application seeds accounts with the weak shared default password 'password123' and stores PII (SSNs, addresses) in the seed data.
SECRET_KEY environment variable is hardcoded in the compose file ('supersecret').
postMessage handler evals event.data.payload without validating event.origin, allowing any embedded page or attacker to execute arbitrary code in the admin app.
URL 'notes' query parameter is rendered via dangerouslySetInnerHTML, enabling stored/reflected XSS via crafted links.
Calculator input is executed with eval() in the browser, allowing arbitrary JS execution from a malicious expression.
Announcement input is appended to the DOM via innerHTML without escaping, enabling DOM XSS.
User search results and the raw search query are interpolated into HTML rendered with dangerouslySetInnerHTML, enabling reflected XSS.
Hardcoded 'admin_master_key_2024' stored as a client-side session secret in localStorage.
